\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اوایل} (avâyel)}{اوایل (avâyel)}]{\fa{اوایل} (avâyel) — early in, the early part}

\label{lesson:FA-C307-avayel}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for during, then the Persian for again.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اوایل}}
\textbf{\fa{اوایل}} (\emph{avâyel}) — \textquotedblleft{}early in, the early part\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اوایل} \fa{بهار} \fa{به} \fa{خانه} \fa{جدید} \fa{رفتیم}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Avâyel-e bahâr be khâne-ye jadid raftim.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Early in the spring we moved to the new house.
\end{quote}

An Arabic broken plural of \emph{avval} \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{}. With the ezafe: \emph{avâyel-e mâh} \textquotedblleft{}early in the month\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{avâyel} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{awā'il}, the broken plural of \emph{awwal} \textquotedblleft{}first\textquotedblright{}, which Persian also has as \emph{avval}. EtymDB lists no entry for the plural.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avâyel}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avâyel}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{avâyel}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for during, then the Persian for again, then say \emph{avâyel} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{اوایل} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Early in, the early part\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اواسط} (avâset)}{اواسط (avâset)}]{\fa{اواسط} (avâset) — the middle of, mid-}

\label{lesson:FA-C307-avaset}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for again, then the Persian for early in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اواسط}}
\textbf{\fa{اواسط}} (\emph{avâset}) — "the middle of, mid-".

\begin{quote}
\fa{اواسط} \fa{تابستان} \fa{هوا} \fa{خیلی} \fa{گرم} \fa{بود}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Avâset-e tâbestân havâ kheyli garm bud.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the middle of summer the weather was very hot.
\end{quote}

Broken plural of \emph{vasat} \textquotedblleft{}middle\textquotedblright{}: \emph{avâset-e hafte} \textquotedblleft{}midweek\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{avâset} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{awāsiṭ}, the broken plural of \emph{wasaṭ} \textquotedblleft{}middle\textquotedblright{}, which Persian also has as \emph{vasat}. EtymDB lists no entry for the plural.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{avâset}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{avâset}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for again, then the Persian for early in, then say \emph{avâset} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اواخر} (avâkher)}{اواخر (avâkher)}]{\fa{اواخر} (avâkher) — late in, the last part}

\label{lesson:FA-C307-avakher}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for early in, then the Persian for the middle of.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اواخر}}
\textbf{\fa{اواخر}} (\emph{avâkher}) — \textquotedblleft{}late in, the last part\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{اواخر} \fa{پاییز} \fa{اولین} \fa{برف} \fa{آمد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Avâkher-e pâyiz avvalin barf âmad.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Late in the autumn the first snow fell.
\end{quote}

Broken plural of \emph{âkhar} \textquotedblleft{}last\textquotedblright{}: \emph{avâkher-e shab} \textquotedblleft{}late at night\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{avâkher} is the Arabic broken plural \emph{awākhir} of \emph{ākhir} \textquotedblleft{}last\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB lists Arabic \emph{ākhir}); Persian also has the singular as \emph{âkhar}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for early in, then the Persian for the middle of, then say \emph{avâkher} again

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{آستانه} (âstâne)}{آستانه (âstâne)}]{\fa{آستانه} (âstâne) — the eve, the threshold}

\label{lesson:FA-C307-astane}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for the middle of, then the Persian for late in.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{آستانه}}
\textbf{\fa{آستانه}} (\emph{âstâne}) — \textquotedblleft{}the eve, the threshold\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{در} \fa{آستانه} \fa{سال} \fa{نو} \fa{همه} \fa{خرید} \fa{میکردند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Dar âstâne-ye sâl-e now hame kharid mikardand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
On the eve of the new year everyone was out shopping.
\end{quote}

\emph{Dar âstâne-ye ...} \textquotedblleft{}on the eve of, on the brink of\textquotedblright{}. Its first meaning is a doorstep.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{âstâne} is inherited from Middle Persian \emph{āstānag} (EtymDB); its first sense is \textquotedblleft{}threshold, doorstep\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âstâne}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{âstâne}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{âstâne}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for the middle of, then the Persian for late in, then say \emph{âstâne} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{حدودا} (hodudan)}{حدودا (hodudan)}]{\fa{حدودا} (hodudan) — roughly, approximately}

\label{lesson:FA-C307-hodudan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for late in, then the Persian for the eve.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{حدودا}}
\textbf{\fa{حدودا}} (\emph{hodudan}) — \textquotedblleft{}roughly, approximately\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{حدودا} \fa{صد} \fa{نفر} \fa{در} \fa{جشن} \fa{بودند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Hodudan sad nafar dar jashn budand.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Roughly a hundred people were at the celebration.
\end{quote}

Also \emph{dar hodud-e} \textquotedblleft{}around\textquotedblright{}: \emph{dar hodud-e sâ'at-e dah} \textquotedblleft{}around ten o'clock\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{hodudan} is built on \emph{hodud} \textquotedblleft{}limits\textquotedblright{}, the Arabic plural of \emph{ḥadd} \textquotedblleft{}limit, edge\textquotedblright{}, with the Arabic adverb ending \emph{-an}. EtymDB lists Arabic \emph{ḥudūd}, \textquotedblleft{}boundaries\textquotedblright{}, though not the adverb.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hodudan}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hodudan}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{hodudan}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for late in, then the Persian for the eve, then say \emph{hodudan} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[(dialogue)]{Telling what happened — a review}

\label{lesson:FA-R307-review-300-307}



\begin{quote}
Say the Persian for suddenly and immediately.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item suddenly, immediately, without delay, the moment that, by chance
  \item to happen, to occur, to come about, to take place, to last
  \item a beginning, to begin, an end, to come to an end, finally
  \item at first, first, then, at the very end, ultimately
  \item at that time, the old days, later on, from then on, recently
  \item dawn, early morning, the next day, the time, round the clock
  \item gradually, meanwhile, until finally, during, again
  \item early in, the middle of, late in, the eve, roughly
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Suddenly? (\textbf{\fa{ناگهان}}.) Immediately? (\textbf{\fa{بلافاصله}}.) Without delay? (\textbf{\fa{بی} \fa{درنگ}}.) The moment that? (\textbf{\fa{همین} \fa{که}}.) By chance? (\textbf{\fa{اتفاقی}}.) To happen? (\textbf{\fa{اتفاق} \fa{افتادن}}.) To occur? (\textbf{\fa{روی} \fa{دادن}}.) To come about? (\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{وقوع} \fa{پیوستن}}.) To take place? (\textbf{\fa{صورت} \fa{گرفتن}}.) To last? (\textbf{\fa{دوام} \fa{آوردن}}.) A beginning? (\textbf{\fa{آغاز}}.) To begin? (\textbf{\fa{آغاز} \fa{شدن}}.) An end? (\textbf{\fa{پایان}}.) To come to an end? (\textbf{\fa{پایان} \fa{یافتن}}.) Finally? (\textbf{\fa{سرانجام}}.) At first? (\textbf{\fa{ابتدا}}.) First? (\textbf{\fa{نخست}}.) Then? (\textbf{\fa{آنگاه}}.) At the very end? (\textbf{\fa{دست} \fa{آخر}}.) Ultimately? (\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{نهایت}}.) At that time? (\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{آن} \fa{زمان}}.) The old days? (\textbf{\fa{قدیم}}.) Later on? (\textbf{\fa{بعدها}}.) From then on? (\textbf{\fa{از} \fa{آن} \fa{پس}}.) Recently? (\textbf{\fa{اخیرا}}.) Dawn? (\textbf{\fa{سپیده} \fa{دم}}.) Early morning? (\textbf{\fa{بامداد}}.) The next day? (\textbf{\fa{فردای} \fa{آن} \fa{روز}}.) The time? (\textbf{\fa{هنگام}}.) Round the clock? (\textbf{\fa{شبانه} \fa{روز}}.) Gradually? (\textbf{\fa{به} \fa{تدریج}}.) Meanwhile? (\textbf{\fa{در} \fa{همین} \fa{حال}}.) Until finally? (\textbf{\fa{تا} \fa{اینکه}}.) During? (\textbf{\fa{طی}}.) Again? (\textbf{\fa{مجددا}}.) Early in? (\textbf{\fa{اوایل}}.) The middle of? (\textbf{\fa{اواسط}}.) Late in? (\textbf{\fa{اواخر}}.) The eve? (\textbf{\fa{آستانه}}.) Roughly? (\textbf{\fa{حدودا}}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
